why_this_matters: Day 229 sits in Phase 12 (Deep Learning + Computer Vision), whose goal is: Understand neural networks from a single neuron to a trained CNN. Today's core material - Beyond accuracy: per-class precision/recall, Confusion matrix analysis, Grad-CAM visualisation - is the vocabulary the rest of the phase is built on. Learners who skip the concept and jump to copying code usually stall two weeks later; the goal here is that you can explain what you did, not just that it ran.

code.heading: **`To print the metrics`**
code.code:
# Creating a dictionary to store the metrics
metrics_dict = {'Model': [], 'Accuracy': [], 'Precision': [], 'Recall': [], 'F1 Score': [], 'AUROC': []}

def assigning_metric_scores(model_name, y_test, y_pred, y_pred_prob):
    model = model_name
    accuracy = accuracy_score(y_test, y_pred)
    precision = precision_score(y_test, y_pred)
    recall = recall_score(y_test, y_pred)
    f1 = f1_score(y_test, y_pred)
    auroc = roc_auc_score(y_test, y_pred_prob)


    metrics_dict['Model'].append(model)
    metrics_dict['Accuracy'].append(accuracy)
    metrics_dict['Precision'].append(precision)
    metrics_dict['Recall'].append(recall)
    metrics_dict['F1 Score'].append(f1)
    metrics_dict['AUROC'].append(auroc)


def print_report_matrix(model_name, y_test, y_pred, y_pred_prob):
    c_report = classification_report(y_test, y_pred)
    print(f"\nClassification Report of {model_name}:\n\n{c_report}")
    # print roc_auc_score
    auroc = roc_auc_score(y_test, y_pred_prob)
    print(f"\nAUROC Score of {model_name}: {auroc:.2f}")


    conf_matrix = confusion_matrix(y_test, y_pred)
    sns.heatmap(conf_matrix, annot=True, fmt='d', cbar=False)
    plt.title(f'{model_name} Confusion Matrix')
    plt.xlabel('Predicted')
    plt.ylabel('True')
    plt.savefig(f'figures/{model_name}_confusion_matrix.png')
    plt.show()

    fpr, tpr, thresholds = roc_curve(y_test, y_pred_prob)
    plt.plot(fpr, tpr, label=f'{model_name} ROC Curve: (AUC_score = {auroc:.2f})')
    plt.plot([0, 1], [0, 1], 'k--')
    plt.xlabel('False Positive Rate')
    plt.ylabel('True Positive Rate')
    plt.title(f'{model_name} ROC Curve')
    plt.legend(loc='lower right')
    plt.savefig(f'figures/{model_name}_roc_curve.png')
    plt.show()

common_mistakes.mistake: Watching the lecture without running the repository notebook.
common_mistakes.why: Recognition is not recall: code that looked obvious fails the moment you type it yourself.
common_mistakes.fix: For every topic today, run the linked notebook cell, then retype it from memory in your own file.

common_mistakes.mistake: Using Beyond accuracy: per-class precision/recall on data whose types or shape you have not printed.
common_mistakes.why: Most failures in this topic are input problems (dtype, shape, missing values) rather than logic errors.
common_mistakes.fix: Print type and shape immediately before the operation; keep that habit for all 275 days.

debugging.symptom: The linked notebook cell raises ModuleNotFoundError or ImportError.
debugging.cause: Wrong kernel/environment selected, or the library is not installed in the active environment.
debugging.fix: Print sys.executable in the notebook and install into that environment (Day 4).

debugging.symptom: Your output differs from the recording even though the code looks identical.
debugging.cause: Library version differences, a changed default argument, or unseeded randomness.
debugging.fix: Pin versions (requirements.txt), set a random seed, and compare dtypes and shapes, not just values (Day 5).
